source.original_title: 05/07/2026 - Larry Ferini & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/07/2026 - Larry Ferini & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Closed

rep.name: Harry Edmonds
rep.location: London, UK; previously spent six months in Korea and has lived in 12 countries in two and a half years

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Taken from the KFS suffix in the title only. Unlike every other KFS call in this batch, the setter is never named or referenced anywhere in the conversation and no notes were read back.

prospect.name: Chris
prospect.aka: Title names the prospect as Larry Ferini; the rep addresses him as Chris twice on the call and the Zoom label is Chris. Surname not established.
prospect.location: Lincolnshire, Illinois, USA — dialling in from Glenview, about 35 minutes north of Chicago
prospect.occupation: Owner-operator of a small business he started recently — electrical or utility field contracting, driving to jobs and setting poles with a skid-steer. No employees. Previously a travelling salesman. Studied in Colorado, lived in Lake Tahoe, spent a year in Korea.
prospect.family_status: Married 13.5 years since 2012; his wife asked for a divorce shortly before the call. One daughter. He will be moving out and selling the house.
prospect.training_background: Gym-goer with no programme — defaults to the treadmill at 10-14% incline until he hits 1,000 feet of climb, about 28-30 minutes, then the sauna. Loves kettlebell work but cannot retain the flows or technique, so he works off Trevor's Instagram reels mid-session and loses his place. Has followed Trevor online for about two years and also watches other kettlebell creators. Long dieting history: 245 lb three years ago, down to 220-225 on Whole30 (which he ran 60-75 days), then down to 190 on carnivore, now back at 210. Has done roughly four extended fasts, the longest 104 hours. Describes himself as a momentum person who writes nothing down.
prospect.medical: Psoriasis on the scalp, elbow and knee, currently unmanaged and actively being self-investigated. States he wants to resolve it through diet specifically to avoid the medical route: 'instead of going to the dermatologist and getting on injections for the rest of my life'. Reports it improved on carnivore and returned when he reintroduced dairy. Experienced cramping and waking with rib cramps on carnivore, which he attributes to mineral deficiency, plus energy collapse and brain fog cycling with diet. Has never had blood work done and has never had a body composition scan. No injuries beyond rolled ankles from skateboarding in high school; describes himself as inflexible and does not stretch.

signals: In the middle of a hard season rather than after one — 'my wife just asked for a divorce' — and framing training as the way through it: 'it's just more motivation to get to the gym and just like get my feelings out and not bottle in'
Reclaiming a self that has been deferred: 'we've been married for 13 and a half years. I've been doing everything for the family. And so now it's time for me to kind of do something for myself'

Cycles of lost and regained ground rather than steady decline — 245 lb, then 190 lb, now 210 lb, with the pattern named by the rep and confirmed: 'you're at two extremes, and the extremes are, I'm all in, and I had bread, everything's over'

Confidence is 0.6 because of a genuine overlap with skeptical_bargain_hunter: he is entirely self-directed, has followed the free content for two years, ran carnivore to a real result at no cost, and arrived expecting 'like a $500 a month kind of a deal'

What separates him from that avatar is that he never disputed the value — 'Everyone's worth more than $6,000... I see the value in it' — his blocker was liquidity during a divorce, not price scepticism

goals.text: A sustainable, intuitive lifestyle he can hold rather than 30-day programmes with an endpoint
Walk into the gym with a game plan instead of scrolling reels between sets
Solve the energy problem so he can actually complete a workout rather than hitting a wall at 12 minutes
Be capable on demand — split a friend's firewood, chase the dog off a coyote, hustle to first base at softball, get through a game of basketball
Be able to do 10 pull-ups without wondering whether he can
Be lean enough to take his daughter and her friends to the pool without being 'the fat dad', and mow the yard shirtless without feeling like an eyesore
Resolve his psoriasis through diet rather than going onto dermatologist-prescribed injections for life
Eat healthily without becoming the outcast at family meals and birthday parties

pains.text: No plan in the gym — 'I don't really have a game plan when I go, so I just usually default to going on the treadmill'
Cannot retain kettlebell flows or technique, so sessions become a frustrating hunt through Instagram reels
All-or-nothing pattern — one slice of bread and 'it's just bad decision after bad decision for the rest of my day'; falls off at Thanksgiving and does not return until March
Energy collapse in the gym on restrictive diets — 'I have zero energy, and it's almost like you kind of feel ill'
Every diet that has worked has been socially isolating — eating steak alone while the family eats something else
Unmanaged psoriasis on scalp, elbow and knee that flares with dairy
Divorce in progress after 13.5 years, with a house to sell, a condo to rent and a daughter in the middle of it
Cash is severely constrained — 'I have more on my credit card than I do on my bank account'
A newly started one-man business that is not yet built up and is only keeping the lights on

objections.raw_quote: how does the structure on payment work? Cause that six grand today seems like crazy
objections.rep_response: Recommended paying up front as a commitment signal, then offered to break it up: 'we don't want money to be the thing that holds you back from having what you want in your life'. Immediately preceded this with the business tax write-off pitch.

objections.raw_quote: it's just hard because I don't have 6,000 in my account right now, and I don't, I have a business debit card, it's a small business, I just started it... it's kind of keeping the lights on in that, but it's not, I haven't built it up yet
objections.rep_response: Offered half and half — $3,000 down with the balance by around the two-and-a-half to three month mark — noting that breaking it down further 'goes up in numbers'. Closed with 'it's supposed to be hard brother'.

objections.raw_quote: It's hard because I'm trying to navigate this, and I'm going to need deposits for apartment or condo, and I've got to, there's just a lot on my plate in this moment because my wife wants to separate
objections.rep_response: Improvised a $1,200 one-month entry — 'I can do something for you where you can get started for 1200, you don't have to pull out 6k or 3k' — with the balance payable by three months to keep the total at $6,000.

objections.raw_quote: I can't make a decision today, Harry. I'm sorry.
objections.rep_response: Reframed the refusal as a language problem — 'It's fine. You can, you're just not willing to. I don't like "I can't" language, Chris. It's limiting yourself' — then told a long personal story about spending his life savings on a mentor, asked where humans grow, and re-offered the one-month entry until the prospect agreed.

objections.raw_quote: I mean, 1,200 right now, like I could throw it on my credit. I have plenty of room on my credit card. It's just scary.
objections.rep_response: Answered with the life-savings story and 'where do we grow man, inside or outside the comfort zone?'

objections.raw_quote: I do deal with psoriasis, I have it on my scalp, my elbow, my knee and I'm trying to figure it out... how do I, if this is also one of my goals, instead of going to the dermatologist and getting on injections for the rest of my life
objections.rep_response: Agreed to run dietary elimination experiments — 'We can test with no dairy. If the psoriasis goes down, great' — while disclaiming expertise: 'I don't think Trevor's like an expert on psoriasis.' Did not suggest seeing a dermatologist.

tiers.note: Rolling monthly rate — 'if you do it monthly it works out to 1200 a month'.

Improvised one-month entry, which is what actually closed: 'I can do something for you where you can get started for 1200... it pays for your first month, next month if you hadn't got all that stuff sorted just be another 1200, and at the end of the three months if you're all good with it you just pay the rest off and it would still be 6k'.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Full up front preferred; or half and half at $3,000 down with the balance by roughly the two-and-a-half to three month mark, keeping the total at $6,000; or rolling monthly at $1,200; or the improvised $1,200 one-month entry with the option to settle the balance before three months to hold the $6,000 total. Rep stated that breaking it down further 'goes up in numbers'.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Implied exit only: 'here's the worst case scenario, if you do one month you finish and you're like, it's impossible for me to continue, okay, but you've had full nutrition, full kettlebells, full mobility, everything's still been created for you, you still have it.'

evidence: Agreed after an explicit prior refusal: 'I can't make a decision today, Harry. I'm sorry.' at 00:58, then 'Let's do it' at 01:05 once the entry price was reduced to $1,200

Rep moved to execution: 'Let's do the onboarding call, let's set you up for the onboarding first, and then we can kind of do the payment, I just remove' — the recording ends mid-sentence as he removes the recorder
Payment method identified as a credit card: 'I could throw it on my credit. I have plenty of room on my credit card. It's just scary.'
Counter-evidence: what closed is a $1,200 one-month entry, not the $6,000 six-month programme — continuation is explicitly conditional on his finances improving in 30 days

Counter-evidence: no payment is confirmed on the recording, no onboarding slot was fixed, and the buyer is mid-divorce with a house to sell, condo deposits to find and, in his words, more owing on his credit card than he holds in his bank account
outcome.next_step: Onboarding call with Trevor to be booked for Monday or Tuesday; $1,200 taken for month one on a credit card, with a review conversation at 30 days about continuing. Full protocols within 24-48 hours of the onboarding call, delivered through the True Coach app.

notable.note: The most flag-dense call in the batch. Identity mismatch: the title names Larry Ferini, the prospect is addressed as Chris throughout. Price fell from $6,000 to a $1,200 one-month entry after the prospect said outright 'I can't make a decision today, Harry' — a refusal the rep reframed as limiting language before telling a personal story about spending his life savings, and the prospect then agreed to put it on a credit card he had just said carries more debt than his bank balance, while mid-divorce and needing housing deposits. The tax pitch reached its most explicit form here: the rep named a client he signed up the previous day, quoted the false invoice description used ('safety and injury prevention program'), and disclosed enough about that client — restaurant brand, three locations, phone area code, state — to identify him. Separately, the prospect wants to manage psoriasis through diet specifically to avoid dermatologist-prescribed injections, and the rep agreed to test it while dismissing blood work as unnecessary and saying he has never had his own checked. Sixth recording in the batch cut at the payment step.

quality.notes: Severe. Labels invert continuously; from roughly 00:20:00 onward whole rep monologues sit under the prospect's label — the flexibility-versus-mobility explanation at 00:22:00, the entire coaching walkthrough from 00:33:11, and the one-month close at 01:05:00 are all the rep's. Several long unpunctuated merged blocks run for two to three minutes each, notably 00:36:19 to 00:39:00 and 00:51:00 to 00:53:21. Attribution of 'It's a $10,000 program. I see the value in it' at 00:58:45 is uncertain between the two speakers and has been treated cautiously. The opening line referencing an 'AI-generated text message thread' is attributed to the rep but the surrounding audio is fragmentary. The file terminates mid-sentence as the recorder is removed.
